# Portfolio website instructions

Use this guidance when working on the personal portfolio website or its project and blog pages.

- Keep the site consistent with its existing static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript structure. Do not introduce a framework, build system, or dependency unless the task calls for it.
- Before changing a page, inspect the related shared layout, navigation, styles, and scripts so the change fits the site's existing patterns.
- Make the smallest complete change, and preserve existing page content, links, and behavior unless the request requires changing them.
- Keep pages usable on small screens and accessible: use semantic HTML, meaningful link text, appropriate headings, and text alternatives for informative images.
- Preserve the existing relative paths and naming conventions when adding or moving pages and assets.
- After editing, check the affected pages and their asset references for broken paths or obvious markup issues. Use only validation tools already present in the repository.
- Do not invent personal, project, or resume details. Ask for clarification if requested content cannot be supported by the existing site or task.
